headline: Korea's unwind went global and the S&P lost 0.1% — because staples and drugs, not semis, are now carrying the index.
summary: Yesterday Korea broke alone. Today it broke everyone in its complex. KOSPI fell another 4.2% to 6114, now -11.9% on the week and -11.5% on the month with z=-1.74 and acceleration z=-1.62; EWY -4.0% on the day, -11.2% on the week. The contagion that did not exist 24 hours ago now does: SOXX -2.6% today and -7.6% on the week, SMH -6.8%, TSM -8.5%, MU -7.0%, AMD -5.9%, ASML -5.9%, and Taiwan finally joined with EWT -3.2% on the week after holding flat yesterday. The index did not care — SPX -0.1% at 7807, 99th percentile; DJI +0.4%. The reason is the new part: the bid rotated into defensives, not cash. XLP +1.2% today and +4.2% on the week, XLU +4.2%, XLV +2.8% with acceleration z=1.14, WMT +7.6% on the week, COST +3.9%, LLY +3.5%, SPLV +0.9%. Staples and healthcare leading with VIX at 15.21 (10th percentile) is a rotation inside a fully invested book, not de-risking — and it is exactly what late-cycle rotations look like before breadth gives way.

The financing side got worse, not better. The 10-year real yield is 2.91%, +45bp on the month, z=1.74 with acceleration z=1.23 at the 97th percentile of the year; nominal 10s at 5.24% (+41bp month), 5s 5.02%, 2s 4.80% and +5bp today even as the long end sat still. The clearest transmission is housing: the 30-year mortgage is 7.40%, +69bp on the month, z=2.06, acceleration z=1.50, the 100th percentile of 52 weeks. ITB is -5.4% on the month at the 0th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile, DHI -8.96% below its 200-day. Rates composite -74. And the dollar printed another high — DXY 102.52, +0.3%, 100th percentile, z=1.72, acceleration 1.64, with EURUSD 1.1171 at the 0th percentile and USDMXN 18.19, +1.2% today and +7.6% on the month, still the single most extreme reading in the book at z=2.84.

What changed in the hedges is the part to sit with. Gold is no longer absorbing any of this: GOLD -0.7% to 4184.7, -5.1% on the month, z=-1.31, 17th percentile and 8.0% below its 200-day; silver -6.8% on the month; GDX -8.8%, GDXJ -10.0%. Meanwhile copper rose 1.3% to 6.73, +4.0% on the month at the 96th percentile, and copper/gold is +2.1% today, +9.6% on the month, z=1.37 at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks. Real yields up, dollar up, gold down, copper up: the market is paying for cyclical ounces of growth and selling the insurance. That is a cleaner cyclical signal than the equity tape, and it argues the semi liquidation is positioning, not demand — WTI +1.4% to 93.10, Brent 105.75, DBC at the 97th percentile, growth pulse +12.

Underneath, the speculative wing keeps draining while credit refuses to. SOL -6.7% today and -14.1% on the week, ETH -4.0%/-9.8%, BTC -2.3% to 81,721, ETH/BTC -7.6% on the month. Breadth stays broken: RSP/SPY at the 11th percentile, IWM/SPY z=-1.50 at the 12th, DJT -4.2% on the month, IYT/SPY at the 7th. Banks have quietly priced a cycle ahead of earnings week — KBE -6.3% and KRE -5.3% on the month, GS -13.1% with z=-1.89, BX -10.7%. Against that, credit composite +42: HYG/IEF at the 94th percentile, BKLN at the 92nd, HYG +0.4% on the week. Breakevens are still falling (5y 2.34%, -7bp on the month; 10y 2.33%) and gasoline fell 4.6% today, so this is a real-rate and dollar squeeze, not an inflation scare. With VIX3M at 17.93 (4th percentile) and MOVE +28.3% on the month, convexity remains the cheapest thing in the book.

good.text: Credit still will not crack: HYG/IEF at the 94th percentile and +0.2% on the month, BKLN flat at the 92nd, HYG +0.4% on the week, credit & vol composite +42. The equity unwind has no funding component yet.

Copper +1.3% to 6.73, +4.0% on the month at the 96th percentile, and copper/gold at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks (+9.6% on the month, z=1.37). Growth pulse +12 says the cyclical bid is real even as semis liquidate.

The defensive bid is funded, not panicked: XLP +4.2% and XLV +2.8% on the week, WMT +7.6%, COST +3.9%, LLY +3.5%, IHI acceleration z=1.76 — with VIX at 15.21, the 10th percentile. Rotation inside the index, not exit from it.

Software and cyber keep taking the semis' money: CIBR +3.6% today, +16.4% on the month with z=2.11 and acceleration z=2.29 at the 100th percentile; IGV +9.6% on the month; PLTR +23.3%; MSFT +9.2% and at a 52-week high.

Brazil is the one unambiguous EM long: BVSP +12.6% on the month (z=2.16) at the 100th percentile, EWZ +14.0%, and USDBRL -0.6% today, -2.3% on the month. Local currency strength plus equity leadership is rare in a 102.5 DXY.

No inflation spiral in the oil move: 5-year breakevens 2.34% (-7bp on the month), 10-year 2.33%, RBOB -4.6% today and -4.9% on the month. Inflation composite -23 keeps the Fed path from getting worse than it already is.

bad.text: Real yields are the whole problem: 10-year TIPS 2.91%, +45bp on the month, z=1.74, acceleration z=1.23, 97th percentile. Nominal 10s 5.24%, 5s 5.02%, 2s +5bp today to 4.80%. Rates composite -74 — the tightening is accelerating, not stabilizing.

The Korea/semi unwind accelerated and spread: KOSPI -4.2% today, -11.9% on the week, z=-1.74 with acceleration z=-1.62; EWY -11.2% on the week; SOXX -7.6%, SMH -6.8%, TSM -8.5%, MU -7.0%, and Taiwan finally cracked (EWT -3.2%).

A 7.40% mortgage at the 100th percentile (+69bp on the month, acceleration z=1.50) is killing the rate-sensitive consumer: ITB -5.4% on the month at the 0th percentile, XHB/SPY 0th percentile, HD -5.9%, MCD -6.7%.
Breadth keeps rotting under a 99th-percentile index: RSP/SPY at the 11th percentile, IWM/SPY z=-1.50 at the 12th and -5.5% on the month, DJT -4.2%, IYT/SPY at the 7th. Breadth composite -16.

The dollar is still making new highs with acceleration z=1.64: DXY 102.52 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.1171 at the 0th, USDMXN +7.6% on the month with z=2.84 and acceleration 2.16, USDCAD z=1.87. Dollar composite -26.

The hedge is failing with the risk: gold -5.1% on the month (z=-1.31, 17th percentile, 8% below its 200-day), silver -6.8%, GDX -8.8%, GDXJ -10.0%. Portfolios losing on both legs is how forced selling starts.

trades.name: Short US housing (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.40% mortgage at a 52wk high, builders at 0th pctile
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy 3-month ITB puts ~5% OTM; cleaner hedged version is short ITB vs long SPY at equal dollars (XHB_SPY as the tracking ratio).
trades.thesis: A 30-year mortgage at 7.40% is +69bp in a month with acceleration z=1.50 and 10-year real yields at 2.91%. Builders cannot buy down rates fast enough at this pace; margins and orders compress before prices do. XHB/SPY and ITB are both at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks and still making new lows — this is a trend, not a washout.
trades.trigger: MORTGAGE30US 7.40%, 100th percentile, z=2.06; ITB -0.9% today, -5.4% on the month, 12.6% below its 200-day; DHI -9.5% over three months; HD -5.9% on the month.
trades.stop: 10-year real yield (DFII10) back under 2.60% or mortgage below 7.00%, or ITB reclaiming its 200-day — cover the position.

trades.name: Long software vs semis (IGV/SMH)
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH: the semi unwind is funding software
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, dollar-neutral. Add CIBR as 25% of the long leg; size to 1x so a semi snapback is survivable.
trades.thesis: The memory/hardware unwind that started in Korea is now global and is a positioning liquidation, not a demand signal — copper at the 96th percentile and credit at the 94th say the cycle is fine. The cash is going to recurring-revenue software and cyber. Despite +8.8% in a week, IGV/SMH still sits at only the 27th percentile of 52 weeks after -45% over a year.
trades.trigger: SOXX -7.6% and SMH -6.8% on the week with TSM -8.5%, MU -7.0%; IGV +1.4% on the week and +9.6% on the month; CIBR +16.4% on the month, z=2.11, acceleration z=2.29, 100th percentile.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.178 (giving up half the week's move), or USDKRW breaking above 1360 signalling the Korea unwind becoming a funding event.
trades.target: IGV/SMH to 0.205 (~+9%), roughly the 50th percentile of the year.

trades.name: Long copper equity vs gold miners
trades.line: Long COPX/FCX vs GDX: copper/gold just hit a 52-week high
trades.expr: Long COPX (or FCX for single-name beta), short GDX, equal dollars. Roughly 60/40 COPX/FCX on the long leg.
trades.thesis: Copper/gold at the 100th percentile with z=1.37 and acceleration z=1.03 is the cleanest growth signal in the book, and gold is failing precisely because real yields are at 2.91% and the dollar is at a 52-week high. The miners have not caught up to the metal: COPX is -3.6% on the month while copper is +4.0%, and GDX is -8.8% on the month with acceleration z=-1.07.
trades.trigger: Copper +1.3% today to 6.73 (96th percentile); copper/gold +2.1% on the day, +9.6% on the month; gold -5.1% on the month, z=-1.31, 17th percentile; GDX/gold -4.9% on the month.
trades.stop: Copper/gold back below its 200-day (a ~15% unwind) or gold reclaiming 4400 — the cyclical read is then wrong.
trades.target: +12% on the pair; COPX back to its 52-week highs as FCX (+3.1% month, 14% above 200-day) leads.

trades.name: Long Brazil vs short Mexico
trades.line: Long EWZ vs short EWW: strong real, a peso nobody has priced
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal dollars. Express the FX alone if preferred: short USDMXN forward vs long BRL, but the equity pair carries the same signal with better liquidity.
trades.thesis: EM is not one trade. Brazil has currency strength and equity leadership simultaneously; Mexico has the most extreme currency stress in the entire digest and an equity market that has discounted none of it. EWW rose 1.8% today while USDMXN rose 1.2% — that divergence closes one way.
trades.trigger: BVSP +12.6% on the month (z=2.16, 100th percentile), EWZ +14.0% on the month, USDBRL -2.3%; against USDMXN 18.19, +7.6% on the month, z=2.84 with acceleration z=2.16, and MXX acceleration z=1.18 into a rolling-over trend.
trades.stop: USDMXN back under 17.50 (the FX stress resolving) or EWZ losing 10% from 43.54.
trades.target: +10% on the pair over the quarter.

trades.name: Buy index convexity
trades.line: Buy Dec SPX puts / VIX calls: VIX3M 17.9 is the 4th pctile
trades.expr: Buy 2-3 month SPX 5-7% OTM put spreads financed by selling a 15% OTM put, or Dec VIX 20/30 call spreads. Keep it a 50-75bp premium outlay.
trades.thesis: You are being handed the cheapest hedge of the year into the most two-sided tape of the year. The index is at the 99th percentile and -0.1% on the day while its biggest growth engine is down 7% on the week and breadth sits at the 11th percentile. MOVE is +28.3% on the month — bond vol is already paying attention; equity vol is not.
trades.trigger: VIX 15.21 (10th percentile), VIX3M 17.93 (4th percentile), term structure 0.848; SKEW 155 at the 81st percentile and +8.4% on the week — tail demand is building while vega stays cheap. MOVE +28.3% on the month with acceleration z=0.94.
trades.stop: Expiry/premium is the stop. Cut early if RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY turn up through their 50-days and 10-year real yields fall 25bp.
trades.target: VIX 25+ on any credit or dollar accident; 3-4x on the call spread.

trades.name: Long healthcare vs consumer discretionary
trades.line: Long XLV vs short XLY: the consumer pays the 5.24% bill
trades.expr: Long XLV, short XLY, equal dollars. LLY and IHI are the acceleration inside the long leg; HD, MCD and NKE are the drag inside the short.
trades.thesis: Healthcare is the only defensive sector with positive relative momentum and real earnings acceleration, while discretionary is caught between a 7.40% mortgage, a 102.5 dollar and a falling discretionary/staples ratio. This is the rotation that actually started today, and it has months to run given XLY/XLP sits at the 14th percentile.
trades.trigger: XLV +0.7% today, +4.4% on the month with acceleration z=1.14 and relative strength turning up; LLY acceleration z=1.10, IHI +2.0% today with acceleration z=1.76. XLY -0.5% today, relative strength -2.4%/-6.9% and in a downtrend; HD -5.9%, MCD -6.7%, NKE -3.9% on the month.
trades.stop: XLY/XLP reclaiming 1.38, or a 30bp fall in 10-year real yields that revives the rate-sensitive consumer.

trades.name: Short crypto beta (MSTR)
trades.line: Short MSTR: SOL -14% on the week, speculative cash draining
trades.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy 2-month puts ~10% OTM. Half size — the stock is +16.6% on the month and will squeeze.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the cleanest read on marginal speculative cash and it is deteriorating faster than the index: the alts are leading down and ETH/BTC is at a fresh low. MSTR is the levered expression, trading 12.6% above its 200-day while BTC rolls and the funding cost of its balance sheet rises with a 5.24% 10-year.
trades.trigger: SOL -6.7% today and -14.1% on the week; ETH -9.8% on the week; BTC -2.3% to 81,721, -4.5% on the week; ETH/BTC -7.6% on the month; MSTR -7.1% on the week with acceleration z=-0.47.
trades.stop: BTC back above 88,000 or MSTR closing above 175.
